user.name: Jim Fan
user.description: NVIDIA Director of Robotics & Distinguished Scientist. Co-Lead of GEAR lab. Solving Physical AGI, one motor at a time. Stanford Ph.D. OpenAI's 1st intern.

fullText:
The sense of touch is the most criminally under-explored modality in robotics. Imagine doing sleight of hand wearing thick oven mitts. That's exactly how a robot feels today if it were alive. A magnetic piece snapping into place, a paper cup peeling out of a stack, a USB negotiating its way into the port - all invisible to the camera.

Learning how to feel must be a full-stack co-designed effort. We are open-sourcing a principled methodology called "T-Rex":

1. Tactile as first-class citizen of the model. Our mixture-of-transformer runs two clocks asynchronously: a slow visuomotor expert plans the motion, and a fast tactile expert refines it in real time with high-frequency corrections at 4 "touch ticks" per vision tick. Forces change faster than frames arrive, so the architecture had to as well.

2. Open data. The largest tactile dataset ever released to our knowledge: a 50-hour (~5,500 episodes) high-quality, carefully synchronized robot play corpus, collected on SOTA tactile hand hardware with 22 degrees of freedom. Available today on HuggingFace!

3. Training recipe: T-Rex extends our prior work, EgoScale. Human egocentric videos for pretraining, a diverse dose of tactile robot play for mid-training. Our experiments show this bridges contact-free pretraining to contact-rich manipulation remarkably well.

Pixels are cheap and everywhere, but they run out of steam at the moment of contact. Tactile will carry the last mile. The next scaling curve will be measured in hours of touch.

fullText:
The next great training dataset may not be a dataset.

It may be a world the model writes for itself.

New paper:

SPADE ♠: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments

Most agents train inside fixed worlds: curated tasks, static synthetic pools or frozen verifiers.

Eventually, the learner catches the curriculum.

SPADE makes the curriculum move.

A single LLM plays two roles:

Environment Designer — writes long-horizon environments as executable Python with an OpenAI Gym-style reset() / step() interface.

Reasoning Agent — enters those worlds, acts across multiple turns and learns from verifiable rewards.

Not generated questions, but stateful environments with transitions, tools, rewards and verification code—one interface spanning reasoning and agentic tool use.

The agent plays each environment with and without a privileged hint. The return gap becomes hint-based regret:

Large gap: solvable with insight, but not yet mastered.

Small gap with high reward: mastery.

Small gap with low reward: probably intractable.

The Designer learns to build worlds at the moving edge of the Agent’s capability—not worlds that are trivial or impossible.

At 30B scale, SPADE reports:

+5.3 points over the strongest fixed-environment baseline across eight held-out benchmarks

+5.7 on BFCL v4 multi-turn

+13.9 on ACEBench-Agent

Its advantage over fixed-environment training grows with model scale.

A broader frontier is becoming visible:

SkillOpt makes skills learnable.

Recirculation makes inference-time architecture adaptable.

SPADE makes the environment itself learnable.

Weights are no longer the only object that can evolve.

Procedures, architectures—and now the worlds that generate experience—can enter the learning loop.

The next scaling law may be the rate at which intelligence creates valid, diverse, executable experiences at its own frontier.

The authors are transparent: generated worlds can be repetitive, flawed or unwinnable. Corpus grounding, environment memory, executable validation and reward-hacking controls are essential.

This is not unlimited self-improvement.

It is a concrete, testable step toward open-ended co-evolution between a learner and the worlds that teach it.

Banger paper from Google DeepMind.

It's on the very hot topic of model routing.

Routers assume the value estimate is free. Working out which specialist handles a query best costs money too, and it is often the larger cost in the pipeline.

This new work formalizes model routing as Pandora's Box, the classic problem of optimal search when inspection is expensive. Under a Gaussian signal model the policies come out in closed form, telling you per specialist and per input whether refining the estimate is worth the price.

Across a multi-LLM benchmark, retrieval-augmented specialists, and LLMs with variable inference-time reasoning, Pandora's Router matches exhaustive estimation quality while calling the expensive estimator far less often.

When competing estimates are noisy, value-of-information reasoning raises the strategic specialist's utility at everyone else's expense.

fullText:
Impressive research from Google on building better environments for agents.

Training environments for agents are hand-built and go stale. The agent improves, the environment does not, and it's not able to see the agent's weaknesses in the first place.

EnvHarness wraps a static environment in a programmable plug-in layer that reshapes its behavior without touching the underlying logic. Every reshaped environment keeps its original verifier; this is what makes the reshaping safe to train on.

EnvRigger treats the policy as a black box, reads its execution trajectories, synthesizes harness components aimed at the diagnosed flaws, then validates them with fresh rollouts.

Across five benchmarks in four domains, up to 9.0 points better on held-out instances with 9.8% fewer execution steps.

fullText:
Wake：以前套壳模型，现在流行套壳code agent，不同Code Agent 聊天记录，现在散在 ~/.claude、~/.codex等多个私有code agent目录里，Wake把这 13 个code  agent 的会话全收进一个窗口，能搜、能跳、能一键接着聊。

它支持的 13 个 agent：

Claude Code、Codex CLI、Copilot CLI、Cursor 的 CLI 转写、OpenCode（含 v2 beta）、Kiro、Gemini CLI、Pi、Oh My Pi、Grok Build、Kimi Code，以及 Antigravity CLI（只能读元数据——转写是加密的）。

痛点：
agent 用久了会意识到一件事：真正积累下来的资产不是代码，是那几百段对话——你怎么描述问题、怎么纠偏、哪条路走通了。但这批资产通常散落在不同地方：Claude Code 在 ~/.claude，Codex 在 ~/.codex，Cursor、opencode、gemini、kimi、grok 各存各的，格式还都不一样，等于每换一个 agent，上下文就清零一次。

Wake 干的就是把这层捡起来：13 个 agent 的 session 只读扫进一个 macOS 原生 app，⌘+K 全文搜索（FTS5 trigram，中文和代码子串同样能搜），选中一条直接回到原目录 resume。

我一直觉得这类"agent 记忆的归集层"会是个独立品类——模型和 agent 会一直换，我们的对话史不该跟着一起丢。它和昨天介绍的 harnessrouter恰好是同一个趋势的两面：HarnessRouter 统一 harness 的"运行"（一套 API 换 harness），Wake 统一 harness 的"历史"（一个窗口看所有会话）。

当一个品类开始出现路由器和聚合器，说明它正在变成基础设施。

Finally a good paper testing whether memory-based self-improving agents actually improve.

The re-evaluation adds two things prior work skipped, multiple runs to measure variance and randomly shuffled task orders.

Both hurt.

Agent evaluation is already noisy on multi-step tasks, and stacking a self-improvement loop amplifies that noise. Default task orderings impose an implicit curriculum that much of the reported gain was riding on.

Adding detailed rubrics and environment feedback to memory construction recovers part of the drop, and a significant gap remains.
